title: Laredo Approves Two Police Grants to Fund Auto Theft Task Force
excerpt: The Laredo City Council approved two state grants totaling more than $3.7 million to fund the police department's auto theft task force through August 2027, covering pay, training and vehicles for 13 officers, according to KGNS.
content:
The Laredo City Council approved two state grants to fund the Laredo Police Department's auto theft task force, according to KGNS.

The grants, from the Texas Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Authority, include $1,904,825 for the Laredo Auto Theft Task Force and $1,829,609 for catalytic converter theft prevention, according to city council agenda documents. The catalytic converter grant carries a $413,964 city cash match, bringing that program's total to $2,243,573. Both grants cover Sept. 1, 2026, through Aug. 31, 2027.

The state funding keeps the task force operating through August 2027, according to the report. Police Chief Miguel Rodriguez said the grants pay for personnel, training and vehicles for 13 officers, and that the city can cancel its Flock license plate reader contract if the money is not appropriated.

Max Prado, with the Laredo Immigrant Alliance, said most of the money goes to surveillance technology, including Flock license plate readers, and called for more transparency, according to the report. “I think one of the council members said it clearly, that the grant applications are very vague, and you know, the more information that the public has, the better off,” Prado said.

The report also noted that nearly 4,000 vehicles belonging to Laredo residents are listed as stolen through the FBI's National Crime Information Center, and that the city had nearly 1,200 vehicles stolen in 2024. The auto theft task force seized 1,040 vehicles in 2023, according to the report.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 18, 2026; City of Laredo council agenda documents, Nov. 16, 2026.
